target: - Cache immutable datasets locally with source/request identity and verified data hashes when iterating. Report measured replay progress; a live process alone does not reveal its stage or prove that database writes did not occur. Historical repository loaders may populate caches, so inspect their actual behavior before calling an entire run read-only.
content:
- For a programmatic ARM audit, run `scripts/research_arm_snapshot.go` together with `scripts/research_arm_data.go` using `go run`, `-conf conf/app.conf`, and an output path outside `temp_strategy`. It parses only the commented `# arm` block, opens exactly `go_binance`, `go_bn_oracle1`, and `go_bn_oracle2`, uses read-only repeatable-read transactions, and can export the database v29 snapshot for semantic comparison. Never edit `conf/app.conf` or use App UI when prohibited.
- For four-year historical replay, run `scripts/research_arm_replay.go` with `scripts/research_arm_data.go`, `-strategy-files`, `-symbols`, `-start`, `-end`, and `-output`; use `-extra-intervals` when a shared cached dataset needs the union of candidate intervals. The loader verifies chunk CRC, exact minute/indicator-bar continuity, archive/ARM overlap, funding coverage, and dataset hashes. Missing monthly-archive bars may be filled only from bounded Binance historical REST responses with exact timestamp continuity; never interpolate or silently accept a gap. Keep large datasets/results in the research cache, not `temp_strategy`.
- Use `scripts/research_generate_variant.go` or `scripts/research_combine_entries.go` only for mechanical generation of full portable candidate JSON under `temp_strategy`; keep their specifications in `research_specs/`. Freeze candidate hash and the unseen coin universe before holdout replay.
